title: Rigid Transformations: Translations, Reflections, and Rotations
seo_title: Rigid Transformations Worksheet: Translations, Reflections, Rotations (Geometry) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on rigid transformations: translation rules, reflections over lines, rotations about the origin, compositions and symmetry. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rigid transformations keep size and shape: the image is congruent.
key_sub: Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Reflect over y = x: (x, y) → (y, x).
body_html:
How it works

A rigid transformation (isometry) moves a figure without changing its size or shape, so the image is congruent. Translations, reflections and rotations are rigid. A reflection changes orientation; the others do not.

  • Translate by (a, b): (x, y) → (x + a, y + b)
  • Reflect over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y)
  • Reflect over the y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y)
  • Reflect over the line y = x: (x, y) → (y, x)
  • Reflect over the line y = −x: (x, y) → (−y, −x)
  • Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x)
  • Rotate 180°: (x, y) → (−x, −y)
  • Rotate 270° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x)

Rotations are counterclockwise unless the problem says clockwise. 90° clockwise is the same as 270° counterclockwise. In a composition, do the first step first; the order can change the result.

Example

Rotate A(3, −5) 90° counterclockwise about the origin.

Rule: (x, y) → (−y, x)

(−(−5), 3)

Answer: A′(5, 3)

Example

Reflect A(6, 1) over the line x = 2.

A is 4 units right of x = 2

Go 4 units left of the line: x = −2

Answer: A′(−2, 1)

Common mistakes

  • Changing the wrong coordinate. Over the x-axis, x stays and y changes sign.
  • Forgetting to swap the coordinates for a 90° rotation or a reflection over y = x.
  • Mixing up clockwise and counterclockwise.
  • Reflecting over x = 2 by changing the sign of x. Measure the distance to the line instead.

faq.q: What is the rule for a 90 degree counterclockwise rotation?
faq.a: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the coordinates and change the sign of the new x-coordinate.

faq.q: What is the rule for reflecting over y = x?

faq.a: A transformation that keeps lengths and angle measures the same: a translation, reflection or rotation. The image is congruent to the original.

faq.q: Does the order of transformations matter?
faq.a: Often, yes. A translation followed by a rotation usually gives a different result than the rotation followed by the translation.

items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (−2, 4). After the second step: (1, 1). The order matters: the other order gives (1, 7).

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular octagon onto itself?
Which transformation does NOT map a square onto itself?
c: A reflection over a line through one vertex and the midpoint of a side
A rotation of 270° about its center
A rotation of 90° about its center
items.e: Squares have 4 lines of symmetry: 2 diagonals and 2 lines through midpoints of opposite sides. A reflection over a line through one vertex and the midpoint of a side.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular 12-gon onto itself?
A point is rotated 360° about the origin. Where does it end up?
c: On the opposite side of the origin
items.e: A full turn brings every point back to where it started. At its starting point.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular pentagon onto itself?
How many lines of symmetry does a regular decagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 10 sides has 10 lines of symmetry. 10.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 8 sides has 8 lines of symmetry. 8.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a isosceles triangle (not equilateral) have?
items.e: Only the line through the vertex angle and the midpoint of the base. 1.

items.q: A figure is reflected over two parallel lines. Which single transformation has the same result?
items.e: Two reflections over parallel lines make a translation, twice the distance between the lines. A translation.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular decagon onto itself?
Which is preserved by every rigid transformation?
items.e: Rigid motions keep size and shape, so the image is congruent. Orientation can change in a reflection. Side lengths and angle measures.

items.q: A figure is reflected over the y-axis and then over the x-axis. Which single transformation has the same result?
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
A rotation of 90° about the origin
items.e: (x, y) → (−x, y) → (−x, −y), which is the 180° rotation rule. A rotation of 180° about the origin.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular 12-gon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 12 sides has 12 lines of symmetry. 12.

items.q: Under a translation, a segment and its image are always
c: Parallel (or on the same line) and the same length
items.e: A translation slides every point the same distance in the same direction. Parallel (or on the same line) and the same length.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram (not a rectangle or rhombus) have?
items.e: No line folds it onto itself, although it has 180° rotational symmetry. 0.

items.q: If a rigid transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle DEF, what can you conclude?
c: Point A and point D are the same point
The triangles are similar but not congruent
The triangles have the same orientation
items.e: Rigid transformations preserve distance and angle measure, so the figures are congruent. The triangles are congruent.

items.q: Which transformation maps a rectangle onto itself?
c: A rotation of 90° about its center
A rotation of 180° about its center
items.e: A rectangle that is not a square only matches itself after a half turn (or a reflection over a line through the midpoints of opposite sides). A rotation of 180° about its center.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 6 sides has 6 lines of symmetry. 6.

items.q: Triangle ABC is rotated 90° about the origin. AB = 7 and m∠B = 48°. What are A′B′ and m∠B′?
items.e: A rotation is rigid, so lengths and angles do not change. A′B′ = 7 and m∠B′ = 48°.
